description: Knicks and Warriors were also in the mix for Ben Simmons
fullText:

The ball is still going to be brought up primarily by Tyrese Maxey, but Maxey already is used to sharing the rock and being effective off of other ball-dominant players. He started his career with Ben Simmons and Joel Embiid. He worked with James Harden for two seasons. Even last year, VJ Edgecombe got touches as a rookie. So Maxey will be sharing playmaking duties with James, without James having to ever over-handle the basketball. It should help everyone in that offense, especially Jaylen Brown, get to a point where they are all efficient and get the ball in places where they can maximize damage. I don't think it happens overnight, but if they get enough games together in the regular season, then Philadelphia's offense has a vast ceiling in the spring. — 8/29/2026 reddit

The Sacramento Kings held a workout for Ben Simmons ahead of his potential NBA comeback, according to Carmichael Dave. "I was told by somebody earlier in the show, not necessarily Kings-related, but you know, somebody who was present at those workouts," he began on SacTown Sports 1140. Sactown Sports 1140: ? NOT A DRILL ? According to @CarmichaelDave , Sacramento Kings GM Scott Perry will be in Florida today to watch free agent G/F Ben Simmons go through a workout? — 8/25/2026 x.com

Fischer expects Simmons to eventually join an NBA team for training camp this fall, but potentially without any guaranteed salary attached. "I'm basically expecting Ben Simmons to be in some NBA team's training camp come this fall," Fischer said. — 8/11/2026 BasketNews

Ben Simmons appears to be teasing a major push to fulfill his plans of an NBA comeback. On Instagram, the former NBA star sparked plenty of reactions with his latest post, which featured a photo of him inside a basketball gym. Simmons said he is proud of where he stands and is "ready for wherever this goes" in the caption. "I wouldn't change the story," Simmons wrote. "The highs, the lows, the pain, the time, the lessons. I embrace all of it. Every chapter built something in me that I couldn't have built any other way. Grateful for where I've been. Proud of where I stand. Ready for wherever this goes." — 8/9/2026 BasketNews

Marc J. Spears: NBA free agent forward Ben Simmons is expected to be a full participant with "zeros restrictions" in a player-led Aussie men's national team mini-camp in Melbourne beginning Monday, sources to @andscape. Simmons took last season off in hopes of completely healing from injuries. The three-time NBA All-Star paid his own way to the camp. A coach who worked out Simmons recently said he has regained his athleticism. The injury-plagued 30-year-old recently told @andscape this is the best he's felt in years. He last played with the Nets & Clippers 24-25 season. Sources: Several NBA teams have expressed interest to Simmons' camp, including one West squad that offered a training camp invite. He is also open to signing a vet minimum contract. Simmons has dreams of playing for Australia during 2028 LA Olympics. Attending mini-camp aids hope. — 8/9/2026 x.com

Simmons seems to be in a good place mentally now, but with all the scrutiny that comes from being Ben Simmons, I wanted to know if there's added pressure for this comeback. "Nah, there's no pressure," he says. "I had pressure when I was injured. People are gonna say the same thing every single time. It's like, All right, well, if that's what you think, then that's what you think." He thinks people are quick to forget the impact he could have on the court in his best moments, the way he contributes in ways that don't show up on a stat sheet. "When I'm out there, I make everybody better. I play defense. I get offensive rebounds." — 6/29/2026 Men's Health

This is why Simmons finds it particularly frustrating when people question his love of the game or his competitiveness, or constantly evaluate his game through the lens of how he once played. "The joy that I play with comes from being healthy," he says. "How do you love something when you're fucked up? How do you love something that you do when you're incapable of doing it?" When I ask Simmons why he didn't just tell people how much pain he was in, he says that he didn't want it to sound like an excuse. "The people I'm closest to, I'll explain it to them," he says. "But at the same time, I don't have the energy to prove it to everybody, you know? And people are gonna make up whatever they want anyway." — 6/29/2026 Men's Health

Ben Simmons says it took him a long time to realize that it was also a nervous system issue. "You can't be in a state where you're in a high-stress situation all the time, especially trying to recover from a back injury," he says. "I would've rather gone through a broken foot again, 'cause it would have been clear and easy." — 6/29/2026 Men's Health

title: Warriors' Jimmy Butler gets eye-opening trade update from ESPN analyst coming off ACL injury
description: The Golden State Warriors have enjoyed having Jimmy Butler over the last couple of seasons. However, there is belief his name will come up at the trade deadline.
fullText:
Warriors' Jimmy Butler gets eye-opening trade update from ESPN analyst coming off ACL injury originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Golden State Warriors are likely to have an up-and-down season this year, no matter how you look at it. The team could struggle early without Jimmy Butler, as he continues to work his way back from injury.

The Warriors lost Butler last season against the Miami Heat, and he ultimately required surgery on his torn ACL.

"Injured Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler underwent successful surgery on his torn right ACL on Monday morning in Los Angeles, the team announced," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote. "Butler suffered the injury on Jan. 19 in a win over the Miami Heat. He consulted several specialists for the surgery, landing on Dr. Bert Mandelbaum, who performed it on Monday morning with a few members of the Warriors' organization on hand."

There is no official timeline for Butler's return, but there is hope that he will be back before the trade deadline.

"If Butler can get back on the floor before the trade deadline, which appears very likely at the moment, this organization will be able to figure out their plan heading into the trade madness and what their playoff outlook is," NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote.

If the Warriors struggle to find success this season, Butler could become an intriguing trade piece. ESPN's Brian Windhorst recently explained why Butler's expiring contract could make him attractive to other teams.

"I know there's been a whole bunch of discussion dating back to last trade deadline about Jimmy Butler. Him coming off the ACL he could function as a huge expiring contract in a trade. I don't think they're operating with day to day. But if player/acquisition comes to the four, they could use that," Windhorst wrote.

Steph Curry and Draymond Green have clearly enjoyed playing with Butler and appreciate what he brings to the team. However, if Golden State can land significant talent in return and use that haul to build around Curry for the final stages of his career, it could be a move worth considering.

Butler would be a valuable piece for any contender, but the possibility of acquiring a strong collection of talent in return could make the Warriors more willing to part ways with him. His future in the Bay Area will be something to monitor closely as the season progresses.

title: Ex-Warriors NBA champion gives Steph Curry retirement prediction with regular season looming
description: The Golden State Warriors have rounded out their roster for the upcoming season. Former Warriors NBA champion, Steph Curry's former teammate just gave a little insight into when he thinks the four-time champion will retire.
fullText:
Ex-Warriors NBA champion gives Steph Curry retirement prediction with regular season looming originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Golden State Warriors know that Steph Curry is nearing the end of his career one way or another. The four-time NBA champion will go down as one of the greatest players to ever play the game.

Golden State and Curry have an important decision to make, as the superstar is eligible for a contract extension.

"What the terms of a new extension look like for Curry will be completely up to him, as the Warriors are prepared to offer their star whatever he wants. If Steph wants the full $136.7 million through the 2028-29 season, he will get that. If he wants to take a discount to help the team, GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. will have no problem with said deal," NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote.

When Curry agrees to the extension will also be important. If he waits, it could potentially benefit the Warriors financially and give the organization more flexibility moving forward.

"There's still players becoming contract extension eligible. By next week you'll start to see Steph Curry's name come up. On the 29th of August he's extension eligible for his contract. I have argued that it should be considered that Steph doesn't sign the extension yet. If he chooses to sign right now, he could get two years at $140 million. Obviously if that's what he says he wants, you give it to him. But if he doesn't sign his contract extension right now the Warriors could have over $100 million in salary cap space next summer," ESPN's Brian Windhorst said.

Curry, like many of the NBA's greatest players, is getting closer to retirement. Former Golden State teammate and champion Matt Barnes recently revealed how long he believes it could be until Curry calls it a career.

"I think Steph is going to ride the ship until it sinks, similar to what Kobe did," Barnes said.

The hope is that the Warriors can make one final championship run before Curry eventually retires. LeBron James is still playing at 41 years old, so Curry could very well want to extend his career for as long as possible as well.

The former MVP remains one of the best shooters in the league, and outside of some injuries, he still looks capable of performing at an elite level. With that in mind, Curry could potentially have another two or three seasons before age begins to significantly catch up with him.

title: Warriors Fans Get Massive Steph Curry Update on Contract Talks and Retirement Plans
description: Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry closed last season on a sour note, falling to the Phoenix Suns in the play-in tournament after Golden State stumbled to a 37-45 finish, its fewest wins since 2019-20. Now entering his 18th NBA season, the four-time champion is opening up about his future in the Bay Area, and [...]
fullText:
Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry closed last season on a sour note, falling to the Phoenix Suns in the play-in tournament after Golden State stumbled to a 37-45 finish, its fewest wins since 2019-20. Now entering his 18th NBA season, the four-time champion is opening up about his future in the Bay Area, and his latest comments carry far more weight than they first appear.

Speaking with NBC Sports Bay Area at the Workday Charity Classic in Palo Alto, Curry made his intentions clear just two days after becoming eligible for a new contract extension.

The 38-year-old guard is entering the final season of his current Golden State Warriors deal, worth 62.6 million dollars, and he is now able to sign a two-year extension worth roughly 136.7 million dollars.

"There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen," Curry said. "The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season, and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity."

The remark leaves little doubt about where Curry sees himself long term, even though the paperwork remains unsigned. General manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. has said Golden State wants a deal finalized before the season begins, but Curry appears content to let the process play out on its own schedule rather than rushing toward a deadline.

Curry's remarks arrive as Golden State tries to move past a rough 2025-26 season that ended with a play-in loss to the Suns. Analysts have questioned whether the current roster can get Curry back to the postseason, though he seems focused on continuity rather than promises.

He is entering his 18th NBA season alongside familiar faces like Draymond Green and Al Horford, with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody working back from knee injuries.

His wife Ayesha shares that same confidence about what comes next for the family. "I think we're going to be in for some fun surprises over the next couple of years," Ayesha Curry added.

Golden State opens training camp at BYU-Hawaii this fall, setting up a preseason slate that will offer the first look at how the roster fits together.

Golden State's preseason schedule opens October 4 against the Los Angeles Clippers, giving fans their first look at this new-look roster. With Curry firmly committed and an extension still pending, the Warriors head into camp focused on health, continuity and getting back into playoff contention this season.

title: Warriors to meet Clippers for preseason game in Hawaii
description: While at training camp in Hawaii, the Warriors are set to meet the Clippers in a preseason contest.
fullText:
On Monday, the Golden State Warriors announced they would be returning to Hawaii for training camp before the start of the 2026-27 regular season. The Warriors have had a tradition of heading to Hawaii for training camp dating all the way back to 1974. In 2024, the Warriors returned to Hawaii for training camp for the first time in 17 years. Now, the Warriors will return to Hawaii again for training camp starting on Sep. 29.

Along with training camp, the Warriors will also play a preseason game in Hawaii for the 15th time. The Warriors won't be alone in Hawaii at the BYU-Hawaii campus. The Los Angeles Clippers will also be in Hawaii for their own training camp. The two teams will meet for a preseason contest on Oct. 4 in Honolulu.

The Los Angeles Clippers and Golden State Warriors will have training camp in Oʻahu, Hawaii and play a preseason game at the University of Hawaii on Oct. 4.

In 2024, the Warriors also played the Clippers, beating Los Angeles 91-90 in Hawaii.

Golden State's contest against the Clippers will mark the start of their preseason on Oct. 4. The Warriors will play five more preseason games, with contests coming against the Los Angeles Lakers, Portland Trail Blazers and Sacramento Kings. The Warriors will return to the Bay Area on Oct. 6 to play the Lakers at Chase Center in the preseason.

After 20 years away, Capcom’s hyper kinetic action adventure returns, pitting skilled samurai Miyamoto Musashi against hordes of warriors and demons in Edo-period Kyoto. Master the complex combat then prepare for flashing blades, disembodied limbs and geysers of spraying blood.

Everything you do in one affects the other in mind-bending ways. The most ingenious puzzle game we’ve seen in a long time.

The team behind the brilliant Marvel’s Spider-Man titles is back with a very different kind of hero. The open-world New York setting is gone in favour of a globe-trotting narrative following Logan on his quest to protect vulnerable mutants. The visuals are gorgeous, while the slick combat brings literal meaning to the term bleeding edge.

The tactical role-playing adventure series returns to the realm explored in the acclaimed Fire Emblem: Three Houses. This time, hopeful contestants arrive at the glorious city of Dagsion to compete in a contest where the winner is granted a single wish. Deep combat, lush settings and fraught relationships are guaranteed.

Silent Hill comes to the east coast of Scotland in a beautifully gloomy new horror adventure. You play as Simon Ordell, returning to a quiet harbour town with no memory of whatever catastrophe has taken place there. The place seems abandoned, but you are not alone for long …

Remedy Entertainment sets out to disprove the notion that all video game sequels are more of the same. title: Agent explains why Jonathan Kuminga rejected Warriors’ $75 million offer
description: Jonathan Kuminga rejected a huge extension to remain with the Warriors, resulting in him now being on the Timberwolves roster.
fullText:
Jonathan Kuminga has had an interesting trajectory in his NBA career, moving on from a chaotic stint with the Golden State Warriors last season. His agent went into detail about what the young forward declined to secure a big extension with Golden State.

Kuminga represented the Warriors for five seasons from 2021 to 2026, winning a title in 2022. However, his final years with the franchise saw him be in and out of the rotation, resulting in frustration over his role. Golden State eventually traded him to the Atlanta Hawks for Kristaps Porzingis.

Kuminga had an opportunity to obtain a three-year contract extension with Golden State for a total of $75 million. However, he declined to sign it as his agent Aaron Turner appeared on the Run It Back podcast to explain the decision.

"Money coming before basketball is not how you continue to make more and more money. … Next year is a way better free agency year for him…teams that have been trying to sign-and-trade for him, like Sacramento and Chicago, will have a lot of money," Turner said.

Mar 1, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Hawks forward Jonathan Kuminga (0) dunks against the Portland Trail Blazers in the fourth quarter at State Farm Arena. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Jonathan Kuminga doesn't have to worry about the Warriors anymore. After all, he is now an official member of the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Timberwolves, which includes a player option on the second season. He chose Minnesota over offers from the Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls and Portland Trail Blazers, via ESPN. Despite the small contract, it's clear that Kuminga wants to maximize his worth as a player in his career for his next deal.

Minnesota finished with a 49-33 record last season, securing the sixth seed in the Western Conference standings. They finished above the Portland Trail Blazers and the Phoenix Suns while trailing the Houston Rockets and the Los Angeles Lakers.

The Timberwolves made noise in the playoffs, stunning the Denver Nuggets in six games despite suffering significant injuries. However, their postseason journey ended after losing to the San Antonio Spurs in six games.

title: Bob Myers shares which veteran urged him to keep Golden State's core intact
description: Former Warriors GM Bob Myers recently shared a story about a veteran urging him to keep Golden State's core intact following a playoff loss (2013-14).
fullText:
Bob Myers, the executive given the most credit for Golden State's four NBA championships from the 2014-15 season to the 2021-22 season, recently took the time to join NBA Hall of Famers Tracy McGrady and Vince Carter on their podcast. Throughout the duration of the episode, Myers revealed many stories throughout his career, discussing what factors led to him leaving the team, what he misses most about the role and the toughest decision he had to make when in charge.

Additionally, Myers shared a story about a veteran player that urged him to keep the roster in tact prior to their eventual dynasty. After winning 51 games during the 2013-14 campaign and losing to the Los Angeles Clippers in Game 7 of the first round of the Western Conference Playoffs, Myers revealed that he received a call from one of the team's most influential veterans, saying, "Jermaine calls me three days after we lost, and I'm thinking he's going to tell me he's retired and whatever. He goes, 'Hey man, listen to me; do not break this team up.' And I was kind of like, what's so great about this team? We just lost in the first round. And he goes, 'I've been in a lot of locker rooms at the end of a season, and this team knows how to lose.' He said it bothered them the right amount."

While O'Neal, a six-time All-Star in his own right, would retire following an 18-year career after that season, the Warriors would begin a historic dynasty the very next year in the 2014-15 campaign.

title: Wigan thrash Hull KR on night of tributes for Boston
description: Wigan Warriors move top of Super League as they thrash Hull KR on an emotional evening as the Cherry and Whites pay tribute to the late Sir Billy Boston.
fullText:
Tries: Marshall 3, Field, Eckersley 2, Keighran, Wardle Goals: Keighran 7

Wigan Warriors moved top of Super League as they thrashed Hull KR on an emotional evening as the Cherry and Whites paid tribute to the late Sir Billy Boston.

The rugby league great, who scored a remarkable 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan and helped them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship during his time with the club, died this week at the age of 92.

Liam Marshall scored a hat-trick of tries as Jai Field, Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran and Jake Wardle all got on the scoresheet in a decent night's work for the hosts.

It was a difficult evening for the visitors who, other than Frankie Dearlove having a second-half try chalked off, offered little in trying conditions with torrential rain making an impact on the playing surface for the second half.

Victory for Wigan means they move two points clear of Leeds Rhinos, while Hull KR remain in sixth and head into their final two games of the regular season two points clear of St Helens in pursuit of the final play-off spot.

A Great Britain international and World Cup winner, Boston was the first black British player to play in Australia and New Zealand when he joined the Great Britain side which toured there in 1954.

Last year, Boston became the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood.

Wreaths were laid and a rendition of Jerusalem was sung in the lead-up to kick-off in tribute to Boston as both sides paid their respects.

Wigan, who wore "Billy" on the front of their shirts thanks to an agreement with their primary sponsor,, external did not take long to get going against Hull KR.

Marshall got Wigan going after nine minutes when he collected Harry Smith's high kick to the corner and another Smith kick soon after sent Field away to score his 100th career try.

Eckersley went in shortly after as Wigan gained ground courtesy of Smith's pinpoint 40/20 kick and he scored his second try just before the half-hour mark after a frantic period in which the hosts somehow kept their attack alive and worked it wide for him to run in at the corner.

Before the first half was out, Marshall put in an acrobatic dive to dot down and Keighran got the second half going.

The Robins fielded a depleted side, with only eight of the 17 from last week's loss to Toulouse featuring in the trip to the Brick Community Stadium, with Jez Litten, Tom Davies and Peta Hiku rested, while Mikey Lewis and Tevita Pangai Jr were still suspended.

It was a shift from earlier this season when Wigan named a heavily rotated and youthful side in a 62-4 defeat in a Super League game, before the two sides met again at Wembley in the Challenge Cup final nine days later.

Dearlove thought he had scored on his KR debut when he slid to the line on a pitch still holding water after an earlier downpour, but his try was chalked off after Bevan French put in an incredible defensive effort to hold the ball up before the young centre could ground it.

Marshall then brought up his hat-trick with relative ease as the game closed out and Wardle put the gloss on a win which means that Leeds, with their vastly superior points difference, will have to beat St Helens on Friday to regain top spot.

Wigan Warriors boss Matt Peet told BBC Radio Manchester:

"It was a fitting occasion for Billy with everything the club did and the atmosphere in the ground.

"I thought the performance was befitting.

"The fans and the people in the crowd who've had a sad week, we have a responsibility."

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters told BBC Radio Humberside:

"I'm really proud of the performance. We had a young side tonight and we didn't stop fighting until the end. We played against a good team, who were extremely disciplined and give you nothing.

"The inexperience we had in this team tonight, the main thing is that we said we need to fight for everything. We gave them a few things but they did the badge proud.

"I've always said players have to earn the jersey, it's not given to them. It was different circumstances tonight and there were probably three players who could have played but they've played a lot of rugby league."

title: ESPN predicts Warriors move up in Western Conference standings next season
description: ESPN predicts that the Golden State Warriors will finish the 2026-27 season with a 35-win campaign, two games worse than their total of 37 last year.
fullText:
The Golden State Warriors had an underwhelming 2025-26 season by many accounts, as injuries to both Jimmy Butler III and Stephen Curry never allowed them to find their footing in a loaded Western Conference playoff race. However, the Warriors were able to sneak into the NBA Play-In Tournament as the No. 10 seed, finishing with a 37-45 record.

Ahead of the 2026-27 season, ESPN recently predicted the records of all 30 teams, and their prediction for Golden State shouldn't come as a shock. ESPN expects the Warriors to finish with a 35-47 record, two wins worse than last year. However, ESPN does predict that a 35-win season will be good enough to move up in the Western Conference standings, passing the Los Angeles Clippers for ninth following the departure of Kawhi Leonard. If Golden State were to win fewer than last year's total of 37 games, it'd mark their worst campaign since the 2019-2020 season, where they finished with 15 victories.

title: Wigan score 11 tries in victory against St Helens
description: Wigan Warriors convincingly beat neighbours St Helens to make it 10 wins out of 10 in the Women's Super League this season.
fullText:
Tries: Williams, Wilson, Jones 2, Derbyshire, Banks 2, Hunter, Foubister, Davies, Salihi Goals: Rowe 6

Wigan Warriors convincingly beat St Helens 56-4 to maintain their 100% winning record in the Women's Super League this season.

Sixteen days after a 44-6 victory in the opening game of the Super Four stage, leaders Wigan scored 11 tries as they dominated once more against their neighbours in the reverse fixture.

Molly Jones and Grace Banks both scored a try in each half, while Anna Davies' late score was Wigan's 10th of the match and took them to the 50-point mark.

title: Wigan beat Wakefield to go top of Super League
description: Jai Field scores a length-of-the-field try to help send Wigan Warriors top of the Super League table with a hard-fought win against Wakefield Trinity.
fullText:
Tries: French, Marshall 2, Field Goals: Keighran 5

Tries: Hall, Rodwell Goals: Jowitt 2

Jai Field scored a length-of-the-field try to send Wigan Warriors top of the Super League table with a hard-fought victory against Wakefield Trinity.

Two quickfire tries from Liam Marshall after Bevan French opened the scoring for Wigan helped put the hosts 20-0 up at break.

And after Corey Hall hit back for Wakefield in the second half, Field hit the visitors on the counter-attack when they spilled the ball just metres short of the try-line as they searched for a second score and a way back into the game.

While Ky Rodwell managed to pull another try back soon after, Wigan confirmed a club-record 12th successive Super League win that edged them above Leeds Rhinos at the summit as Wakefield remain in fourth.

Leigh thump Bradford to move closer to play-offs

How the table looks could change drastically by the end of the weekend, with Leeds able to reclaim top spot if they beat York Knights on Sunday, while a third successive Trinity loss has them in danger of dropping to fifth on Saturday if defending champions Hull KR beat Toulouse Olympique.

Both sides had early chances to take the lead, but French was the reason that neither of them managed to open the scoring in the first 10 minutes.

First the Australian wasted a golden opportunity to send Zach Eckersley over with a forward pass, but within two minutes he came up with a stunning try-saving intervention at the other end by holding Max Jowitt up over the line before the full-back was controversially judged to lose the ball in his attempt to touchdown.

Eventually, it was French himself who broke the deadlock, pouncing on a stray Wakefield pass inside his own half before sprinting 65 metres untouched to go in near to the posts.

Two tries in five minutes from Marshall out wide put Warriors in a commanding position before the half-hour mark.

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell called on Emre Guler for the first time soon after that, with the prop coming off the bench just two days after his move from NRL side St George Illawarra Dragons was brought forward by Trinity.

It was only five days ago that Guler, who had been due to make his Super League move next season, had started for the Dragons in their win against Wests Tigers.

Wakefield threatened to respond a number of times before Hall plucked a searching high ball from Jake Trueman from the sky to dot down for the visitors in the 53rd minute.

Hall very nearly linked up with Jowitt for another Wakefield four-pointer soon after, but the centre was forced into touch by Eckersley as he dished the ball off for the finish.

The game's definitive moment came in the 65th minute when Field swooped on a knock-on from Mike McMeeken, who was within barging distance of the try-line, allowing the full-back to race away 95 metres in the other direction to score his 15th Super League try of the season.

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet told BBC Radio Manchester:

"I'm really pleased. We were against a good team that threw a lot at us. I liked our effort, particularly defensively. I thought second half we weren't great with the ball, but I loved our defence.

"The crowd was fantastic again, there was great energy in the stadium and it was a good game - particularly in the first half when it was going set for set."

[On being top of Super League after making it 12 successive wins] "It's irrelevant, really. It doesn't mean a lot.

"It's boring isn't it, but we take each day as it comes. There are plenty of those games where we could have got beaten, so we won't get too carried away."

Wakefield Trinity head coach Daryl Powell told BBC Radio Leeds:

"I thought we were immense tonight. At 20-0 at half-time, it was the least likely 20-0 scoreline I've ever seen in my life. I thought we started the game unbelievably well and then we gave them a try.

"We've lost three games now, and I am disappointed, but I'm actually really enthused by what I saw tonight.

"I do think the refereeing department has to ask themselves a couple of questions, because that is ridiculous that first decision [to deny Jowitt a try]. Out of tonight, both teams were top class but there are other parts of this game that weren't.

"I'll be asking my team to get better from tonight and I think they should be doing the same."

title: Wigan score six tries to hammer wasteful Bradford

High-flying Wigan Warriors moved alongside Leeds at the top of the Super League table, putting on an outstanding defensive performance to defeat a one-dimensional Bradford Bulls at Odsal.

Following a slow start, Wigan took control of the game with scores from Jake Wardle, Adam Keighran and Bevan French before half-time, as Bradford struggled to generate opportunities.

After the break, the Warriors maintained their dominance as Wardle, Kian McDermott and Jake Kerr added further scores, with Andy Ackers claiming the sole consolation for the home side.

The result strengthens Wigan's position in second, behind Leeds only on points difference now, while Bradford remain 13th, two points ahead of bottom-of-the-table Huddersfield.

Looking to keep their strong recent record against their hosts intact, Wigan found their rhythm after an attritional opening.

Wardle did the honours, seizing on the loose ball before fighting his way through two weak Bulls tackles to score the first try of the game.

It did not take long for the visitors to extend their lead.

Following an unsuccessful Bradford attack, the Warriors made quick ground up the field. On the final tackle, and with the try line beckoning, French found Keighran who powered over.

Bradford went close to equalising soon after, only for referee Marcus Griffiths to decide that Chris Atkin had been held up over the line after good work from Joe Mellor.

With the game broken up by stoppages and penalties, Wigan had to wait well into the second quarter for their third.

In a pre-worked move, Harry Smith sent a pinpoint kick up for French to chase. The Australian timed his jump perfectly, beating Caleb Aekins to the ball to dot down.

Immediately after the break Wigan thought they had scored again, only to have the try called back with Patrick Mago adjudged to have knocked on in the act of scoring.

Not to be denied for long, the visitors then capitalised on an error from Ackers with Wardle ultimately benefiting as the Bradford defence found itself out of shape.

McDermott then got in on the action, running in untouched as the home defence tired, after quick interplay between Smith and French.

Ackers finally got the Bulls on the board, fighting his way through a series of Wigan tackles, but it was little consolation after a frustrating afternoon.

title: Young starlets power Ontario past Ashland in season opener
description: Three of the Warriors' four goals came from a freshman and sophomore.
fullText:
ONTARIO - Coach Larry Atkinson and his staff wondered where the goals would come from this fall.

"That was our big question," he said. "We had everybody back on defense — plus a girl that hasn't played the last couple years back — so we knew we'd be solid there.

"Where are we going to get the shots from? Where are we going to get some goals from?"

ARROWS RUN RAMPANT! Ashland boys soccer routs Ontario in emphatic season opening win

It took just 30 seconds for Ontario to record its first shot on goal Friday evening and less than nine minutes to put the ball in the back of the net for the first time in the Warriors' 4-2 win over Ashland.

"I think we came out really strong," freshman Keatyn Kilgore said. "We have some stuff to work on because it's the beginning of the season, but I feel like we came out strong and put it together. But we have a lot to work on still."

There is a lot to work on, sure. But there's a lot to be impressed with already with Kilgore netting a brace, senior Braelyn Llewellyn and sophomore Mia Moton also joined in on the scoring, and Maia Fox had an assist.

"We had a chance to score a goal in the first 30 seconds ... and I think we had 20 shots on goal, which is a lot," Atkinson said. "We have to get more efficient, but the field was sloppy and that hurt us because we have speed. We like to move the ball and it just wore them out because you're stepping into something deep, you're going down in the ground, it's hard on your legs, but we persevered and got through it.

"Then every time we scored, they would come back. We finally got the two-goal lead and kept that ... we made a goalie mistake and we can't have that, can't give anybody a free goal. But overall, for our first game after the summer we've had, I'm very pleased."

Llewellyn opened the scoring in the 9th minute before Kilgore doubled the advantage in the 26th. Just before the half, though, Ashland junior Mia Gonzalez pulled one back tapping in a cross from senior Aliviah Sauder. Moton finished off a counterattack four minutes into the second half to restore the two-goal lead before Gonzalez struck again two minutes later. Kilgore latched onto a through ball from Fox in the 58th minute as a buffer goal, and the Warriors would then lean on defense to close out the win.

"We could have had a lot more goals, we just need to work on some stuff and our finishing," Kilgore said.

"We missed some shots we should have made, but we'll chalk it up to nerves for the first game or the conditions," Atkinson added. "We have a week to get ready for Lexington and see what we need to work on."

For the Arrows, there's a lot coach Lee Hunt wants to work on after the first match.

"We started a little slower than I wanted to," he said. "There were some bright spots in the game at times ... we'll go back to work this week before we play again Thursday."

Gonzalez's brace was the highlight for Ashland and flashes of the team's potential were on display.

"There's a lot of could have on this team, there's a lot of reasons to be excited for what this team can do throughout the season," Hunt said. "It's a long season and this is just game one."

description: Try-machine Zach Eckersley and Liam Marshall both score twice as Wigan Warriors beat Toulouse Olympique 48-18 to go second in Super League.
fullText:
Tries: Eckersley 2, French, Marshall 2, Hodkinson, Eseh, Field Goals: Smith 8

Tries: Ulberg, Tropis, Rouge Goals: Rouge 3

Try machine Zach Eckersley and Liam Marshall both scored twice as Wigan Warriors overpowered Toulouse Olympique 48-18 to make it 11 wins in a row to climb to second in Super League.

Eckersley took his try tally for the season to 33 and Bevan French was also magnificent at the Brick Community Stadium, scoring once and creating another for Jai Field.

Harry Smith kicked eight goals from eight, while Noah Hodkinson and Sam Eseh also went over for the relentless Warriors, who went up through the gears in the second half.

Toulouse had their moments and fought back to level 18-18 just before half-time as they scored through Paul Ulberg, Romeo Tropis and Cesar Rouge.

Ruthless Wire crush Bulls to go fourth

Huddersfield thrash Catalans to mark Dewsbury move

Wigan had suffered shock home losses to Castleford Tigers and Huddersfield Giants this season and Toulouse opened the scoring after just four minutes when Ulberg cut inside from the right to go over.

But the hosts responded in the 10th minute when Eckersley punched a hole in the Toulouse line to register their opening score.

Wigan's second try eight minutes later was all about the brilliance of French. The Australian half-back jinked his way over for a fine try to score for the fourth successive game and take his points tally for Wigan to 501.

Toulouse conceded too many penalties and Wigan crossed for their third try when they passed the ball along the line for Marshall to score on the left.

Wigan also displayed frailties and Toulouse cut their lead to six points on 29 minutes when they scored from only their second attack when Brendan Hands played a grubber kick through for Tropis to touch down.

And four minutes later they added another try when Rouge's kick came off Smith and the Frenchman collected the ball to score.

Wigan responded two minutes before half-time when Hodkinson powered over on the right for his 15th Super League try of the season.

Again Toulouse conceded a needless penalty when they had Wigan under pressure, allowing the Warriors to move upfield with Hodkinson playing the ball inside for Eckersley to score his second try of the game.

The home side put some daylight between themselves and Toulouse on 51 minutes when Eseh came off the bench to power through three tackles to score under the posts.

Brad O'Neill was sin-binned four minutes later for a dangerous tackle, but there was no stopping Wigan and their 12 men held firm before French broke and kicked for Field to score.

Wigan were rampant and Marshall crossed for his second try on 78 minutes to complete a comprehensive victory.

Wigan head coach Matt Peet told Sky Sports:

On Bevan French: "Sometimes we brush over that and talk about the small things he does and the team things he does, but the fact is, he's one of the players we have and they're the reason the stadium is full. They're the reason we're enjoying ourselves at the moment.

"We've got talent, him, Harry [Smith], Jai [Field]. They're getting the balance right between giving them the freedom to express themselves and getting the boring stuff right."

On winning 11 games in a row: "I think any team can decide if they finish the season positively or not. We'll concentrate on tomorrow and take it week by week.

"The season certainly, when you zoom out is looking exciting and competitive and we wouldn't want it any other way."

title: Lakers Could Add Klay Thompson Following Latest Update
description: Former Warriors guard Klay Thompson has long been connected to the Lakers, but it seems more possible than ever that he could join LA. The post Lakers Could Add Klay Thompson Following Latest Update appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
Former Golden State Warriors guard Klay Thompson has long been connected to the Lakers, but in the twilight of his career, it seems more possible than ever that he could join LA.

Thompson has a natural connection to the Lakers, being the son of Mychal Thompson, a longtime Laker and true fan favorite.

Klay was a mainstay with the Warriors for a very long time, and even when he hit free agency, he chose to sign with the Mavericks rather than join the Lakers, passing up a real chance to join LA.

Recently, Mychal shared that he is "trying" to get Klay to sign with the Lakers, joining Doncic in LA this time and serving as a shooter on the wing.

While Klay is not currently a free agent, he is under contract for one more year, earning $17.4 million. There are rumors of a possible buyout or trade away from the Mavericks, looking to help a team on a contender.

After talk of a buyout, the Mavs reportedly want to instead work out a trade to avoid paying part of Thompson's salary and possibly get any kind of assets.

Thompson, a three-point shooting specialist, has gone through knee and leg injuries that have sapped a good part of his athleticism.

His play was so poor upon his comeback that the Warriors and Thompson made the call to move on.

The Dallas Mavericks, looking to get over the hump in the postseason with Luka Doncic, decided to pursue Thompson and signed him to a big free-agent contract.

However, things changed quickly for the Mavs; they ended up trading Doncic and going through a full rebuild, and they are now led by second-year player Cooper Flagg.

With the Mavs, Thompson has still shot the ball well, though his points have been on a decline, along with his field goal attempts per game.

Last year, he played 69 games, started only eight games, and put up 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.

Thompson, one of the greatest shooters of all time, shot 39.1% in 2024 and 38.3% last year from deep.

The Lakers need help on the wings, and a change of scenery, alongside an established role on a competitor, could be what Thompson needs to get his career going again.

At 36 and with so many surgeries, he may not have much juice left, but if he does, the Lakers could use him.

LA may be more willing to sign him following a buyout rather than trade for him, but they will likely be inquiring to see how viable adding Thompson is.

title: Warriors Get Intriguing Anthony Davis Update Amid Stephen Curry Decision
description: Golden State passed on an aggressive Anthony Davis pursuit this summer, but two looming contract decisions could change the conversation. The post Warriors Get Intriguing Anthony Davis Update Amid Stephen Curry Decision appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Anthony Davis is not available. At least not yet.

The Washington Wizards have given no indication they intend to trade him, and the Golden State Warriors did not come particularly close to acquiring him when they explored the possibility earlier this offseason.

Still, Davis' future suddenly carries more uncertainty than it did when Washington shut down trade interest in June.

The Wizards and Davis have mutually agreed to table negotiations on a potential four-year, $275 million extension until the regular season, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday on NBA Today. One source told Charania the sides want to let approximately 20 games "marinate" before deciding whether their partnership should continue through a new contract.

For Golden State, the development is worth monitoring. Its championship window around Stephen Curry continues to narrow, and Davis was central to the Warriors' most ambitious offseason scenario before LeBron James signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.

GettyStephen Curry of the Golden State Warriors shoots over Anthony Davis and LeBron James of the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on January 27, 2024 in San Francisco, California.

Golden State planned to pursue James in free agency and explore a trade for Davis, Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor reported in June. Washington had no interest in listening to offers, preventing those plans from gaining traction.

The Warriors also had internal reservations. According to The Ringer's Logan Murdock, a small group within Golden State's front office supported trading Jimmy Butler and draft capital for Davis. The organization ultimately declined to push forward because of Davis' injury history and desire for a lucrative extension.

Davis' fit beside Curry remains obvious. His screening, lob finishing and ability to punish switches would give Curry an elite pick-and-roll partner. Defensively, Davis could protect the rim while allowing Draymond Green to roam, switch and direct traffic.

Davis averaged 20.4 points, 11.1 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 20 games for Dallas last season. But hand and groin injuries ended his campaign before he could debut for Washington, reinforcing the concerns that kept Golden State from making a more aggressive push.

If Davis becomes available, Golden State cannot assemble a deal from spare contracts.

Butler's expiring $56.8 million salary is the Warriors' only clean, single-contract match for Davis, who will earn approximately $58.4 million this season. That financial reality — not necessarily a demand from Washington — would make Butler the practical foundation of almost any Davis trade.

The alternative would be a more complicated package constructed around the combined salaries of Green and Kristaps Porziņģis.

Green re-signed on a one-year, $27.7 million contract after opting out to help Golden State pursue James. Although signing a one-year deal created implicit veto rights, Green waived that protection in favor of a 15% trade kicker, according to ESPN's Anthony Slater. He becomes eligible to be traded Dec. 15 and would receive a bonus of approximately $4.2 million if moved.

The Warriors have maintained that they do not intend to trade Green. His contract, however, preserves their ability to do so if a franchise-altering opportunity emerges.

That flexibility matters because Curry's future is also approaching a decision point. The 38-year-old guard is under contract only through 2026-27 and becomes eligible Aug. 29 for a two-year extension worth up to approximately $136.7 million. ESPN has reported mutual interest in another agreement.

But Curry's contract cannot be separated entirely from the roster around him. Butler is recovering from a torn ACL, Green is 36, and Golden State won only 37 games last season.

Washington's first 20 games will determine whether Davis fits alongside Trae Young, Alex Sarr and AJ Dybantsa. They could also determine whether Golden State gets another opportunity to make the aggressive move it passed on this summer.

This time, the Warriors would know exactly where the money must come from.

title: Wigan thrash Saints in opening Super Four game
description: Wigan Warriors kick off the new Super Four format of the Women's Super League with a thumping 44-6 win at St Helens.
fullText:
Tries: Derbyshire 2, Hunter 2, Davies, M Jones, Wilton, Foubister, Coleman Goals: Rowe 4

Wigan Warriors maintained their 100% record in 2026 as they comfortably saw off rivals St Helens in the first match of the new Super Four format.

It was a fifth successive win for them over Saints in the past 12 months, including a 54-6 demolition in the Challenge Cup final at Wembley, as they underlined why they are the team to beat in the Women's Super League.

The defending champions scored nine tries with two apiece for Ellise Derbyshire and Eva Hunter with further scores from Anna Davies, Molly Jones, Remi Wilton, Jenna Foubister and Mary Coleman at the BrewDog Stadium.

St Helens were outclassed on home turf and had only a Luci McColm try on the stroke of half-time on a difficult evening.

Whatever the format, though, there is no doubt that Wigan are the standard-bearers for the rest to catch.

They scored from their first set as a high kick into the sun on the last tackle was spilled by young Saints full-back Liv Leach and bounced invitingly for Derbyshire to score.

That was soon backed up by a fabulous individual try from Woman of Steel Hunter as she received the ball inside her own half and showed an irresistible combination of power, pace and sidestepping to score.

To make matters worse for Saints, Leach had to be carried off the field and by the 15th minute the contest was nearly over as Davies went over in the corner after a gorgeous kick over the top from Izzy Rowe.

Derbyshire and Hunter crossed for their second tries and only a poor conversion rate from Rowe prevented Wigan from being out of sight.

With this, Saints finally gained some possession and repeat sets and McColm went over just before the interval.

However, hopes of any kind of comeback never materialised as Jones' try on her first appearance of the season after a knee injury got Wigan moving again.

And the champions simply were too hot to handle in the final quarter as Wilton, Foubister and Coleman went over as Denis Betts' side picked up from where they had left off in their last match nearly four weeks ago.

This was the opening match in the new Super Four format introduced for the 2026 season.

After seven rounds of games, with all sides playing each other once, the league has been split into a top four and a bottom four although all points have been carried forward.

There are now six rounds of games over the next six weekends with home-and-away fixtures against the other three teams in their section in an attempt to have the best teams playing each other more often to increase competition and intensity.

So Wigan play Saints, Leeds Rhinos and York Valkyrie twice, with the side who finishes top at the end of that securing a direct place into the Grand Final, second and third having a play-off to decide who else reaches that game and fourth missing out completely.

Meanwhile in the Shield, for the sides from fifth to eighth after seven matches, the side finishing bottom at the end of the season will play the winners of the National Championship for the final remaining Super League spot in 2027.

fullText:
Warrington Wolves and Wigan Warriors are set to meet in Dublin in 2027 in the first Super League fixture to be played in Ireland.

The two teams will face each other at the newly refurbished Laya Arena, home of rugby union side Leinster, on Saturday, 24 April 2027.

"This is another landmark moment for our club, for Super League and for the sport of rugby league," Warrington chief executive Karl Fitzpatrick said.

"Following the success of the Las Vegas and Paris projects, and the appetite shown for taking our game to new audiences, Dublin is the perfect next destination.

"It is a world-class sporting city with a proven track record of hosting major international events and provides another outstanding opportunity to showcase our sport on the big stage."

The fixture marks the second time Warrington and Wigan have met in Dublin, having previously faced off at Shelbourne Park in 1934 - while Wigan also played against Leeds in a Charity Shield fixture in Dublin in 1995.

It also marks another milestone in Super League fixtures taking place outside of the sport's heartlands, as the pair met in the inaugural Rugby League Las Vegas event in 2025, while Wigan also faced Catalans in Paris earlier this year.

Wigan Warriors chief executive officer Kris Radlinski added: "Hopefully this will become another successful chapter in rugby league's growth story and show what can be achieved when we're prepared to think differently and be ambitious."

The 20,000 capacity Laya Arena has undergone a €52 million transformation before its reopening in August, in the lead up to the 2026 Dublin Horse Show.

Next year's fixture is primed to take place in the week before next season's Magic Weekend event, which is set to begin on Saturday, 1 May.

"Dublin has an outstanding reputation for hosting major sporting events and provides the perfect stage for two proud clubs and two passionate sets of supporters to showcase everything that makes our game special," Radlinski added.

"This is about creating an occasion that people want to be part of, whether they're lifelong supporters or discovering rugby league for the very first time."

title: Warriors Timeline to Make Trade for Stephen Curry Help Updated
description: The Golden State Warriors are in the depths of a disappointing summer. Will they get trade help for Stephen Curry? The post Warriors Timeline to Make Trade for Stephen Curry Help Updated appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
After a summer in which the Golden State Warriors pretty much stood pat on a roster that was knocked around by injuries and wound up with a 37-win record and an ouster in the play-in tournament, frustration among the team’s fan base is running high. The only discernable plan for the team was to try to lure LeBron James in free agency, a plan that the team apparently felt had little hope of succeeding all along. Stephen Curry will turn 38 next season, and could be a free agent next summer.

The front office, though, is not showing much urgency in putting together a roster.

The Warriors have tools to be more active on the trade market, but the issue is, using those tools is unlikely to make the team good enough to truly contend in the West, especially with an array of health questions on the roster–both Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are rehabbing knee surgeries, Curry himself is still getting over a late-season bout of runner’s knee and Kristaps Porzingis is iffy every game.

But there is a timeline, it seems, of what the Warriors might see that would inspire them to pull the trigger on a big move.

That’s according to Anthony Slater, the Warriors’ beat writer for ESPN. Speaking on 95.7 The Game in San Francisco on Thursday morning, he said that it is wrong to assume Golden State will not trade picks to bolster the team now. But trading picks for a team that can’t stay healthy would be foolish.

If the Warriors’ young players show promise and the veterans get and stay healthy, a move could be coming.

Said Slater: “For Stephen Curry, moving forward, I think what is most important for him is to make sure that knee and body are as right as possible as he enters his age 38 season. Try to be as healthy and productive early on as possible. I think collectively as a team, Steve Kerr mentioned, there is some belief they can have some internal growth and maybe even surprise early in the season.

“And I think the better they are in the first couple months, the healthier Steph Curry looks, the more likely it is that this front office can be convinced to trade to try and upgrade the roster.”

Now, all of that might sound too hope-based to persuade Warriors fans out of their state of frustration. It requires the Warriors to get lucky with some young players, stay healthy and get their current guys back.

But, Slater said, that is pretty much how Curry sees things. The front office will let the season unfold, and perhaps a trade will follow.

Slater continued: “As Jimmy Butler gets closer and closer to a return, as Moses Moody gets closer and closer to a return, as they have a lot of expiring deals and they still have some tools out there, maybe Yaxel Lendeborg takes a leap—that is the theory, if you’re Steph and you want to take the optimistic approach. And Steph is an optimistic guy. What can he do? If you get closer to the deadline, maybe you do something, maybe you don’t, but I think they will be further motivated if the team looks like they’re not just fading into the abyss.

When the Warriors were eliminated in April, there was some thought this could be a major offseason of change in the Bay Area.

Green has agreed to a one-year, $27.7 million deal to return to the Warriors, ESPN's Shams Charania reports.

title: ‘Truly a Joke’ — NBA World Rips Warriors Owner Joe Lacob’s Controversial Decision to Focus on ‘Post-Steph Curry Era’
description: The Golden State Warriors’ offseason plan to give Stephen Curry another shot at the championship did not go as planned. After LeBron James decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Warriors insider Tim Kawakami reported on Saturday that team governor Joe Lacob has shifted his focus past the Curry era.
fullText:
The Golden State Warriors’ offseason plan to give Stephen Curry another shot at the championship did not go as planned. After LeBron James decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Warriors insider Tim Kawakami reported on Saturday that team governor Joe Lacob has shifted his focus past the Curry era.

Unsurprisingly, Kawakami’s report sparked a major buzz in the NBA world.

The Warriors’ offseason began with grand visions of landing James after Draymond Green declined a $27.7 million player option to create salary-cap flexibility.

The plan met a major snag as the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar reportedly wanted the Warriors to sign Washington Wizards center Anthony Davis, whom the Wizards were unwilling to trade.

Still, the allure of joining forces with Curry delayed James’ decision before the four-time MVP eventually signed with the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday.

From trying to build a legendary lineup, Lacob has seemingly quit on the Warriors’ franchise icon. According to Kawakami, the billionaire will rebuild in the “post-Steph Curry era.”

The viral report drew strong reactions from the WNBA community.

“What a shame. Steph Curry is still one of the best players in the world. To not make an effort to win another title with him is truly a joke. And if you’re not gonna do that, then you have to trade him. Instead, the Warriors are just wasting Steph’s final years. So sad,” NBA analyst Kevin O’Connor tweeted.

“Stephen Curry gets to finish his career where and when he wants. The Warriors can’t trade him unless he asks them to. But in pure basketball terms, it’s better for everyone if he asks for a trade. Golden State’s window is closed, and he’s too good for an extended retirement tour,” CBS Sports’ Sam Quinn added.

“Bro, they doing Steph dirty like that,” an X user wrote.

“They wasted the last 7 years just lucked into 1 championship, so it’s not talked about,” another X user added.

“Joe Lacob has been trying to build post Steph for 8 years now. He brought in a bunch of draft picks (that all sucked) for a post Steph era only for Steph to win the Championship despite this,” another user added.

With James going East, the Warriors’ biggest offseason move left is likely re-signing Green.

After retaining Kristaps Porzingis and De’Anthony Melton and adding Charles Bassey, Golden State’s roster is practically set for the 2026-27 season.

So, the Warriors, which finished this past season with a 37-45 record, will start the new campaign without Butler and Moses Moody. While both rehab from injuries, the Dubs are desperately hoping the oft-injured Porzingis stays healthy, the 40-year-old Al Horford provides quality minutes, and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg contributes.

Meanwhile, the Oklahoma City Thunder are stronger than ever and are looking to regain their crown. The San Antonio Spurs not only gained valuable playoff experience but also retooled.

Other contenders like the Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves have also made major offseason moves, making the stacked West even more competitive.

Lacob is essentially asking the 38-year-old Curry to keep a hobbled, aging roster afloat, a rinse-and-repeat situation that has often ended in disappointment for the superstar point guard and the team.

Until Curry retires or asks for a trade, this could be the familiar scenario Dubs Nation will be looking at.

title: Warriors Trade Idea Swaps Podziemski for Elite Sharpshooter, Steven Adams
description: This Warriors trade sends Brandin Podziemski and Moses Moody to the Rockets in exchange for Reed Sheppard and Steven Adams. The post Warriors Trade Idea Swaps Podziemski for Elite Sharpshooter, Steven Adams appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Even the most loyal Golden State Warriors fan would admit that Brandin Podziemski hasn’t developed at the pace the franchise expected him to. At the end of his rookie season, the southpaw was widely heralded as Stephen Curry’s successor. Three years in, he has seemingly plateaued into an average rotational piece.

With Podz set to hit restricted free agency next year, the Warriors may be better off moving him before they have to grapple with a Jonathan Kuminga-type situation.

One Warriors trade idea doing the rounds would see the Bay Area franchise part with Podziemski and Moses Moody, who is expected to miss the first half of the 2026-27 season with injury, for a haul from the Houston Rockets.

Warriors would receive: Steven Adams, Reed Sheppard

Rockets would receive: Brandin Podziemski, Moses Moody

The hypothetical move stands to help both teams, as we explain below.

The return of Fred VanVleet from injury means Reed Sheppard will likely go back to a bench role after the young sharpshooter had a difficult playoff series against the Los Angeles Lakers. In the six-game series, the former No. 3 overall pick averaged 12.2 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.2 steals, but shot a paltry 30% from the field and 29% from three. While he averaged 32.2 minutes, Sheppard lost the faith of Rockets head coach Ime Udoka, who preferred to end games with either Tari Eason or Josh Okogie.

Much like the Warriors and Podz, the Rockets may run into a similar financial issue with Sheppard, who has only one more guaranteed year left before hitting restricted free agency in 2028. After extending Eason recently, the Rockets are also on the clock with Amen Thompson, who will hit restricted free agency in 2027.

Moody, who has two years left on a budget-friendly deal, isn’t a huge risk for the Rockets in this scenario. Ditto with Podz, whom they can simply waive next year.

Reed Sheppard has a lot of untapped potential, with some analysts projecting him to be an elite sharpshooter for years in the NBA. As a shooter, who better to harness your craft under than Stephen Curry, the greatest shooter in the history of the sport?

For all his flaws — including his defensive lapses and poor late-game decision-making — Sheppard is one of the purest young shooters in the NBA. In two seasons, he has drained 275 threes at a clip of 38.3% — elite numbers for a 22-year-old. A movement shooter who can also shoot off the dribble, he will fit nicely in Golden State’s system.

As for Steven Adams, the Warriors could use some interior presnece after finishing 22nd in rebounding and 26th in blocked shots last season. Adams will also bring the sort of toughness and physicality that the Warriors sorely miss when defensive anchor Draymond Green goes to the bench. In recent years, they’re unable to impose themselves defensively even when Green, 36, has been on the court.

title: Warriors Proposed to Land Trey Murphy in 3-Team Trade As LeBron Moves On
description: With LeBron James dream nearly dead, this Warriors trade pitch lands Trey Murphy III, the Bay Area franchise's coveted "dream" target. The post Warriors Proposed to Land Trey Murphy in 3-Team Trade As LeBron Moves On appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Amid increasing chatter of LeBron James narrowing his free-agency options to the Miami Heat and Cleveland Cavaliers, the time has arrived for the Golden State Warriors to explore other avenues to improve their roster around Stephen Curry and Draymond Green.

Enter Trey Murphy III: a player who has hovered on the Warriors’ radar for years and remains a widely cited “dream target” who could now be up for grabs.

According to The Athletic’s John Hollinger, rival teams are expected to gauge the New Orleans Pelicans‘ willingness to trade the sharpshooting wing once the LeBron James free-agency sweepstakes conclude.

“Chatter about a Trey Murphy trade, while lessened, hasn’t vanished and is one of many potential pieces of league business that could resurface once LeBron James’ next destination becomes clear,” Hollinger reported on Monday.

Amid the reports, a Warriors trade idea doing the rounds would see the franchise part with Brandin Podziemski, Moses Moody and multiple first-round picks (the Pelicans are reportedly seeking up to three) in order to land Murphy.

Warriors would receive: Trey Murphy III

Pelicans would receive: Moses Moody (via NTMLE), Myles Turner, unrestricted 2027 first-round pick (via GSW), 2029 first-round pick (via GSW) and 2031 first-round pick (via GSW)

Bucks would receive: Brandin Podziemski

Some would argue that giving up three first-round picks, Podz and Moody just for Murphy is an astronomical asking price. Unfortunately for the Warriors, they’re in a desperate situation as Stephen Curry will turn 39 midway through the 2026-27 season, and Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III aren’t getting any younger.

A player like Murray — who thrives as a movement shooter — will obviously be the ideal fit next to Curry, Butler, Green and Porzingis, forming a potent starting five.

It’s also now widely accepted that neither Podziemski nor Moody have established themselves as key pieces of Golden State’s future core, making them dispensable.

The Pelicans were forced to bring Zion Williamson off the bench last season due to their frontcourt logjam, which includes Herbert Jones, Derik Queen, Yves Messi and Saddiq Bey. At some point, Murphy will likely be better off playing elsewhere, especially if not being utilized to the best of his abilities in New Orleans.

Also, the Pels don’t hurt their future at all by grabbing three first-round picks from Golden State. The move would actually open up the possibility of the franchise trading other veterans like Williamson, Jordan Poole, Dejounte Murray and Jones, and giving the keys to their coveted young duo of Queen and Jeremiah Fears.

One of the few teams still flush with cap space, the Bucks have nothing to lose by onboarding Podziemski, who hits restricted free agency next year. If Podz doesn’t gel with their young core of Ryan Rollins, Brayden Burries, Nate Ament, Kel’el Ware, Kasparas Jakučionis and Jaime Jaquez Jr, they can simply let him walk next year.

The southpaw has definitely flashed enough potential in his three years in Golden State to get a look-in from the Bucks or any other young team.

title: Vegas Summer League Notebook: Like all good things, the Lakers run has come to an end
description: LAS VEGAS – Heading into their Summer League semifinal clash against the Golden State Warriors on Saturday, the Los Angeles Lakers seemed almost invincible.
fullText:
LAS VEGAS – Heading into their Summer League semifinal clash against the Golden State Warriors on Saturday, the Los Angeles Lakers seemed almost invincible.

The Lakers were the only remaining undefeated team at 4-0, playing good, efficient and — most importantly — winning basketball while downing teams by an average margin of victory of 17.5 points.

However, just like Goliath had David, every giant eventually stumbles into its kryptonite. For the Lakers, that was this Warriors squad — ever so game and extremely well-drilled defensively. Golden State grinded out a 92-88 win at Thomas & Mack Center to advance into Sunday’s championship game, where they will face the Memphis Grizzlies.

“They’re a very good team, very disciplined,” Lakers’ second-year guard Chris Manon said. “I think they had a very good game plan going in, and they made adjustments throughout the game as well. It was a good battle.

“Unfortunately, they had our number, and we can’t get [this one] back. But hopefully in the future, maybe in the G League, maybe [in the NBA], we’ll get them back.”

Overall, the matchup was as closely contested as could be. There was no separating the two sides at any point, right up until the end. And in such games, the finest of margins prove decisive. This time was no different.

While both teams shot sub-50 percent from the field, the Warriors found an edge from three-point range — going 12-for-24. The Lakers were only able to convert six of their 27 attempts.

Golden State guard Chance McMillan did a stellar job of stretching the floor for the Warriors. He went 4-for-4 from three for 12 of his 14 points in three quarters. As a result, the Warriors were able to punish the undersized Lakers inside down the stretch. Big man Graham Ike was the biggest beneficiary with a 16-point, 11-rebound double-double. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg (15) and LJ Cryer (16, 4-8 3PT) combined for 31 points.

Lakers’ second-year forward Adou Thiero chose the perfect time to turn in a breakout performance to lead his team. However, his 18 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, and three steals on 6-for-6 shooting (1-1 3PT, 3-3 FT) were not enough.

Rookie first-rounder Cameron Carr added 17 points despite never really finding his shooter’s touch (5-16 FG, 1-8 3PT). Manon posted 10 points, seven rebounds, and four assists. He shot 3-for-9 and contributed with two steals and one block on defense.

Though they came up short of the ultimate finish line, the Lakers can’t say they didn’t have their chances to pull out a win in the dying embers. A victory would’ve sent them to their first Summer League championship game since 2018. They won it the year prior.

Trailing by six with 1:45 remaining in the fourth quarter, the Lakers were handed a lifeline when Ike was assessed a technical and a flagrant one after a hard foul on Arthur Kaluma. But Los Angeles could only go 1-for-3 on the ensuing free throws.

Moments later, however, Thiero got to the cup for a deuce, and Carr nailed both of his free throws — after drawing a foul off a Kaluma steal — to make it a one-point game with 1:12 left to play.

And the craziness wouldn’t end there. After both teams exchanged sloppy turnovers, the Warriors extended their lead back to three right before Manon was fouled on a three-pointer with nine seconds remaining. With an opportunity to tie the game, the undrafted guard went 2-for-3 at the line, leaving the Warriors in the driver’s seat.

Golden State was then able to ice it at the opposing charity stripe, courtesy of a pair from McMillan and a split from Will Richard.

The defeat for this high-flying Lakers team was gutting. However, once the dust settles, the consensus belief is that the experience gained will be priceless.

“We were one of four teams playing for something,” Summer League head coach Ty Abbott said. “In those high-pressure moments where not only are they pressuring you on the floor but you know you’re playing to win, it’s either win or you go home, to be able to have the game in the balance and it’s on you to handle the ball and get us in an action, get us organized, try to get solid possessions to score, that builds a lot of confidence regardless of the outcome.”

Manon and Carr echoed Abbott’s thoughts. Naturally, the goal was to go all the way — especially because of how well the roster had gelled together over the summer. But the most important thing in these games is always growth with one eye on the big picture — that being the NBA.

“That was real basketball right there,” Manon said. “Most of the time you’re going to be in close games, and you have to be calm and able to execute. It’s unfortunate that we only got [one close game] and we lost it, but it’s a good learning experience nevertheless.”

Carr added: “It’s important to continue to learn and grow. Like I said [before], I can only be where my feet are right now, and we just lost the game, so I [will] go [back] to the drawing board and keep growing and learning as a player.”

Jim Lenihan's side made a nonsense of the fact they had suffered 11 straight defeats going into the game and threatened to do the league double over the in-form Warriors after pulling off a shock victory at the Brick Community Stadium in March.

Taane Milne's try put the league's bottom side ahead, but Oliver Partington and Eckersley hit back with tries which had Matt Peet's team 10-4 up at the break.

The hosts raised their game again in the second half to level through Jacob Gagai but as their discipline faltered and Joe Greenwood was sin-binned for dissent, Adam Keighran's penalty and a late Eckersley double secured the win for Wigan.

Huddersfield have suffered another tough week, losing three players for the season through injury and having long-serving chairman Ken Davy step down, and the sight of Wigan rolling into town on the back of seven successive wins in all competitions had some supporters fearing the worst.

Lenihan has started to work a little magic, however, and after Huddersfield soaked up the expected early pressure, they struck first as Milne finished strongly.

Wigan have been in imperious form and they soon edged ahead as Partington stretched out to finish after evading two tackles following Keighran's short, sharp pass.

Tanguy Zenon was forced off with a head injury after being knocked out cold, and Eckersley took advantage of a brilliant Keighran pass to score his first try of the evening and open a six-point gap at half-time.

Tempers flared throughout the game and referee Matty Lynn's patience ran out just before the interval as he sent both Tui Lolohea and Shea O'Connor to the sin-bin for a tussle at the play-the-ball.

It started to look like the game would slip away from Huddersfield, but they muscled up again in the second half and levelled when Gagai finished a slick passing move and George Flanagan, on as the 18th man, kicked the extras.

Suddenly it was Wigan who looked unsure of themselves, but the game turned on moments of indiscipline.

Huddersfield thought they had scored a brilliant counter-attacking try after Wigan's teenage half-back George Marsden had dropped the ball, but referee Lynn disallowed it for a forward pass.

To rub salt in the wound, Wigan challenged the decision and were awarded a penalty for a high challenge on Marsden, with Keighran converting the two points to restore the lead.

Huddersfield were still hunting the win but when they were penalised for a knock-on, Greenwood disputed the decision despite the captain's challenge having been used, and he was sent to the sin-bin.

That ended the superb Huddersfield effort as Wigan went up the other end and Harry Smith, the calmest man on the pitch, dinked a beautiful kick for Eckersley to race through and collect for his second try.

With all resistance over, Eckersley claimed his hat-trick, and made it 19 tries for the season, from George O'Loughlin's pass on the last tackle.

Campbell double sets up St Helens win over Catalans

Huddersfield Giants coach Jim Lenihan told BBC Radio Leeds:

"I'm certainly very proud of the boys. Our effort was pretty good and went deep into the game with an opportunity to win, and then obviously just fell away at the back end.

"They only scored two tries at the back end when they sent one of us off again.

"Our effort was pretty good but it's something we always have to be working on and it has to get better.

"It's not a moment where you suddenly have a good weekend at it and you can just focus less on it. It's a constant evolving state, and something we have to keep taking steps at."

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet told BBC Radio Manchester:

"I'm proud of the players for showing the resolve to get the two points. Huddersfield pushed us all the way. It was a game we could have lost.

"We did some uncharacteristic things but managed to come out the other side of it, mainly because of the tenacity of the group.

"We are a little bit light on troops and it's a different experience for those young players, but I'm just glad to get away with two points."
